'''Stewart Sanders Adams''' {{post-nominals||country=GBR|size=100%|OBE}} (16 April 1923 – 30 January 2019) was an English [[pharmacist]], and [[Biological engineering|bioengineer]] who was part of a team from [[Boots UK|Boots]] which developed the painkiller [[ibuprofen]] in 1961. Ibuprofen is now on the [[World Health Organization]]'s [[WHO Model List of Essential Medicines|Model List of Essential Medicines]] and is one of the world's best-selling drugs.<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/university/colleges/mds/news/2016/05/Midlands-research-powerhouse-will-use-powerful-new-imaging-technology-to-develop-the-next-generation-of-drugs.aspx |title=Midlands research powerhouse will use powerful new imaging technology to develop the next generation of drugs |publisher=[[University of Birmingham]] |date=12 May 2016 |accessdate=3 February 2019}}</ref>

==Early life==
Adams was born in [[Byfield, Northamptonshire]], at 4 New Terrace (later re-numbered as no. 7) on 16 April 1923.<ref>{{cite news|last=Davison |first=Phil |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/obituaries/stewart-adams-british-pharmacist-who-helped-create-ibuprofen-dies-at-95/2019/02/05/9b5db304-2643-11e9-ad53-824486280311_story.html |title=Stewart Adams, British pharmacist who helped create ibuprofen, dies at 95 |newspaper=The Washington Post |accessdate=2019-02-09}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|date=January 2012|title=An interview with Stewart Adams|url=https://www.cell.com/trends/pharmacological-sciences/pdf/S0165-6147(11)00194-5.pdf|journal=[[Trends in Pharmacological Sciences]]|volume=33|issue=1|pages=1–2|doi=10.1016/j.tips.2011.10.007|pmid=22338705|last1=Adams|first1=S.}}</ref> His father was a railwayman, and grew up in a rural farming area in [[Northamptonshire]].<ref name="telegraph">{{Cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/health/3351540/Dr-Stewart-Adams-I-tested-ibuprofen-on-my-hangover.html|title=Dr Stewart Adams: 'I tested ibuprofen on my hangover'|last=Lambert|first=Victoria|date=8 October 2007|work=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]}}</ref> Adams was an only child.

Adams went to Byfield Council School, then his parents moved in 1933 to [[Doncaster]], and he went to [[Hall Cross Academy|Doncaster Grammar School]], then in 1937, to [[March, Cambridgeshire|March]], [[Isle of Ely]], where he attended [[March Grammar School]]; he left school aged 15 in 1939.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nottinghampost.com/School-Days-Dr-Stewart-Adams/story-19359796-detail/story.html|title=My School Days: Dr Stewart Adams|work=[[Nottingham Post]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=March marks centenary of the birth of ibuprofen creator |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-cambridgeshire-65263499 |access-date=16 April 2023 |work=BBC News |date=16 April 2023}}</ref>  He became a [[pharmacist]], on a three-year [[apprenticeship]], at a [[Boots UK|Boots]] chemist in March. From this he gained an interest in science, and Boots paid for him to do a [[Bachelor of Pharmacy|B.Pharm]] degree at [[University College, Nottingham]], which he was awarded in 1945.

==Career==
[[File:Ibuprofen.svg|thumb|right|250px|Structure of the ibuprofen [[Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug|NSAID]] ]]
He rejoined the Boots company in 1945 and worked on their project to produce [[penicillin]]. He was moved to the research department of Boots and he went on to research [[rheumatoid arthritis]]. This was followed by a PhD in [[pharmacology]] at [[Leeds University]] returning to Boots in 1952.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/health-34798438|title=The hangover that led to the discovery of ibuprofen|date=15 November 2015|work=[[BBC News]]|accessdate=15 November 2015}}</ref> It was funded by a £600 research scholarship from the [[Pharmaceutical Society]] that was matched by Boots and focussed on the heparin-histamine relationships.<ref name="Leeds alum invented ibuprofen">{{cite web|url=https://www.alumni.leeds.ac.uk/ibuprofen?srctid=1&erid=6716161&trid=160373c4-4db8-4961-ba87-075b4663603f|title=Leeds alum invented ibuprofen|website=Leeds Alumni Online|publisher=[[University of Leeds]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160309224932/https://www.alumni.leeds.ac.uk/ibuprofen?srctid=1&erid=6716161&trid=160373c4-4db8-4961-ba87-075b4663603f|archive-date=9 March 2016|url-status=dead|accessdate=9 March 2016}}</ref> At the time, the main medicine for the condition were [[corticosteroid]]s and high doses of [[aspirin]], which had such side effects as [[Gastrointestinal problem|gastrointestinal problems]] and [[allergic reactions]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Rainsford |first1=Kim D. |title=Ibuprofen: a critical bibliographic review |date=2003 |publisher=Taylor and Francis Ltd |location=London |isbn=978-0-2033-6258-7 |page=5}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.invent.org/inductees/stewart-adams|title=Stewart Adams {{!}} The National Inventors Hall of Fame|website=www.invent.org|language=en|access-date=2020-01-26}}</ref>

===Ibuprofen===
[[File:RSC Ibuprofen synthesis.png|thumb|right|How to make 2-(4-isobutylphenyl) propanoic acid]]
At the Boots Pure Drug Company in 1953, Adams began work on other chemical substances that could have a pain-killing effect, centred on [[rheumatoid arthritis]]. He worked in a house in the south of Nottingham for many years, as the main labs had been destroyed in the war, then moved to Boots Pharmaceuticals new building on Pennyfoot Street in 1960. This is now [[BioCity Nottingham]].

In August 1958 on Rutland Road in [[West Bridgford]],<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=yEhuuidCJ7IC&pg=PA5 Ibuprofen: A Critical Bibliographic Review]</ref> the team, with [[Brasenose College, Oxford|Oxford]]-educated organic chemist [[John Nicholson (chemist)|John Nicholson]] (1925–83),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bnc.ox.ac.uk/about-brasenose/news/1244-brasenose-chemist-honoured|title=Brasenose Chemist Honoured|publisher=[[Brasenose College]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190113064242/https://www.bnc.ox.ac.uk/about-brasenose/news/1244-brasenose-chemist-honoured|archive-date=13 January 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=CAcLCgAAQBAJ&pg=PA10 Ibuprofen: Discovery, Development and Therapeutics]</ref> looked at [[Alkoxy group|phenoxy]] acids. In 1961 the team started looking at [[Phenylpropanoic acid|phenyl-propanoic acids]], and things were looking good. One of the types was 2-(4-isobutylphenyl) propanoic acid; ibuprofen was first made in December 1961.

Four substances that went to [[clinical trial]] failed, and the last – ibuprofen – worked; it was first called RD 13621, and RB 1472. He took the first dose himself and used the drug to treat his own headaches before it was on the market. Animal tests were very encouraging, and tests on humans showed it was about three times stronger than aspirin. He had read in a German journal about ultra-violet-induced [[erythema]] on the skin of shaved guinea pigs discovered by [[Parke-Davis]], so he could test [[anti-inflammatory]] treatments; the [[Ultraviolet|UV-light]] came from a [[Ernst Kromayer|Kromayer Lamp]]. Some drugs had had amazing effects on [[Albinism|albino]] guinea pigs, but none on humans. It had low [[Gastrointestinal bleeding|GI toxicity]] in dogs. Boots also now wanted the new chemical to reduce fever (an [[antipyretic]] effect). The work was supported in the 1950s by the Empire Rheumatism Council (now [[Arthritis Research UK]]). The first clinical trials were by Dr. Tom Chalmers at the Rheumatic Diseases Unit at the Northern General Hospital, Edinburgh (which closed around 1990) in 1966.

===Licensing===
A [[patent]] was filed in 1962, and granted in 1962, for [[Phenyl alkanoic acids|phenylalkane derivatives]]. In 1969 ibuprofen was licensed as a [[prescription drug]] in the UK, and in 1974 in the US. It was launched in the US in 1974 by [[Upjohn]] of [[Kalamazoo, Michigan]], as ''Motrin''. In April 1966, Ibufenac (iso-butyl-phenyl-acetic-acid, known as ''Dytransin'') went onto the UK market, but was withdrawn in January 1968 due to causing jaundice, from its toxicity in the liver.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Rainsford |first1=Kim D. |title=Ibuprofen: a critical bibliographic review |date=2003 |publisher=Taylor and Francis Ltd |location=London |isbn=978-0-2033-6258-7 |pages=20–27}}</ref>

===General pharmacies===
In August 1978, Boots applied to have ibuprofen put in general pharmacies, but the [[Committee on Safety of Medicines]] (DHSS) declined; in April 1982, there was another request by Boots. Ibuprofen became on sale for general pharmacy ([[Over-the-counter drug|over-the-counter]]) in 1983, as [[Ibuprofen brand names|Nurofen]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Rainsford |first1=Kim D. |title=Ibuprofen: a critical bibliographic review |date=2003 |publisher=Taylor and Francis Ltd |location=London |isbn=978-0-2033-6258-7 |pages=18–19}}</ref> Adams said in 2007 "Getting the drug approved by the two countries with the toughest regulatory authorities – the UK and the US – was a goal I wanted to achieve. For me, that was the most exciting time of all."<ref name="telegraph" /> Nurofen was launched 8 August 1983 by [[Crookes Healthcare|Crookes Products Ltd]]. Ibuprofen went over the counter in the US in June 1984 by the [[Food and Drug Administration]], made by [[American Home Products]]. In America, it was made by [[Whitehall Laboratories]], known as Advil, and also sold as ''Nuprin''.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Rainsford |first1=Kim D. |title=Ibuprofen: a critical bibliographic review |date=2003 |publisher=Taylor and Francis Ltd |location=London |isbn=978-0-2033-6258-7 |page=20}}</ref>

Adams retired as Head of Pharmacological Sciences at Boots in 1983.<ref name="Leeds alum invented ibuprofen"/> For ibuprofen, Boots received the [[Queen's Awards for Enterprise|Queen's Award for Technological Achievement]] in 1985.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Rainsford |first1=Kim D. |title=Ibuprofen: a critical bibliographic review |date=2003 |publisher=Taylor and Francis Ltd |location=London |isbn=978-0-2033-6258-7 |page=21}}</ref>

==Recognition==
===Inventors Hall of Fame===
In 2022, Adams was inducted into the [[National Inventors Hall of Fame]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Stewart Adams: Ibuprofen |url=https://www.invent.org/inductees/stewart-adams |website=invent.org |access-date=11 May 2022}}</ref>

=== Blue plaques ===
[[File:Ibuprofen Blue Plaque, BioCity, Nottingham 01.jpg|thumb|The [[List of blue plaques erected by the Royal Society of Chemistry|Royal Society of Chemistry blue plaque]] at [[BioCity Nottingham]] ]]

In November 2013 work on ibuprofen was recognised by the erection of a [[List of blue plaques erected by the Royal Society of Chemistry|Royal Society of Chemistry blue plaque]] at Boots' Beeston Factory site in Nottingham, which reads:<ref name="rsc">{{cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/AboutUs/News/PressReleases/2013/ibuprofen-chemical-landmark.asp|title=Chemical landmark plaque honours scientific discovery past and future|date=21 November 2013|publisher=[[Royal Society of Chemistry]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180927004543/http://www.rsc.org/AboutUs/News/PressReleases/2013/ibuprofen-chemical-landmark.asp|archive-date=27 September 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

{{Quote|In recognition of the work during the 1980s by The Boots Company PLC on the development of ibuprofen which resulted in its move from prescription only status to over the counter sale, therefore expanding its use to millions of people worldwide}}

and another at [[BioCity Nottingham]], the site of the original laboratory, which reads:<ref name="rsc" />

{{quote|In recognition of the pioneering research work, here on Pennyfood Street, by Dr Stewart Adams and Dr John Nicholson in the Research Department of Boots which led to the discovery of ibuprofen used by millions worldwide for the relief of pain.}}

===Dr Stewart Adams Bridge===
A new pedestrian and cycle bridge connecting the Nottingham Science Park to the Boots head office campus, over the [[Midland Main Line]], was named after Adams, as part of the [[Midland Main Line upgrade|electrification works]].<ref name="TransportNotttm-20200309">{{cite web |title=Bridge named after Boots chemist who helped discover Ibuprofen |url=https://www.transportnottingham.com/bridge-named-after-boots-chemist-who-helped-discover-ibuprofen/ |website=Transport Nottingham |publisher=Nottingham City Council |access-date=12 February 2022 |date=9 March 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He married Mary, a teacher, in 1950, just before he moved to [[Leeds]] where he was introduced to [[Rugby league]]. He lived in [[Redhill, Nottinghamshire]], in the house he moved into in 1955,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nottinghampost.com/Stewart-Adams-man-discovered-ibuprofen/story-17635696-detail/story.html|title=Stewart Adams, the man who discovered ibuprofen|date=20 December 2012|work=[[Nottingham Post]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140729005549/https://www.nottinghampost.com/Stewart-Adams-man-discovered-ibuprofen/story-17635696-detail/story.html|archive-date=29 July 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> in the north of [[Nottingham]]. He became a Freeman of the City of Nottingham in 2013.<ref name="citycouncil">{{cite web|url=https://committee.nottinghamcity.gov.uk/Data/City%20Council%20(Extraordinary)/20130708/Agenda/CouncillorChapman%20-%2057200.pdf|title=Nottingham City Council – City Council Extraordinary Meeting|date=8 July 2013|publisher=[[Nottingham City Council]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181215222927/https://committee.nottinghamcity.gov.uk/Data/City%20Council%20(Extraordinary)/20130708/Agenda/CouncillorChapman%20-%2057200.pdf|archive-date=15 December 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> Adams was appointed an [[Officer of the Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) in the [[1987 New Year Honours]].<ref name="citycouncil" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thegazette.co.uk/London/issue/50764/page/9|title=Supplement to The London Gazette of Tuesday, 30th December 1986|date=31 December 1986|work=[[The London Gazette]]|issue=50764|page=9}}{{dead link|date=July 2020|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} [https://archive.org/details/LondonGazetteNo50764 Alt URL]</ref>

Adams died aged 95 at the [[Queen's Medical Centre]] on 30 January 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nottinghampost.com/news/business/inventor-ibuprofen-created-boots-nottingham-2490268|title=Dr Stewart Adams, who invented ibuprofen in Nottingham, dies at the age of 95|last1=Bunn|first1=Matthew|date=31 January 2019|website=[[Nottingham Post]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190201165509/https://www.nottinghampost.com/news/business/inventor-ibuprofen-created-boots-nottingham-2490268|archive-date=1 February 2019|url-status=live|accessdate=31 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2019/feb/13/stewart-adams-obituary|title=Stewart Adams obituary|last=Ferry|first=Georgina|date=2019-02-13|work=The Guardian|access-date=2019-02-18|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077}}</ref>
